threats.abuse_case: A caller replays another tenant or sponsor identifier and receives memory candidates across the server-derived scope boundary.
Untrusted captured content is promoted into durable memory without attributable evidence or independent human acceptance.
A credential, client payload, or raw transcript crosses the synthetic and redaction boundary into stored memory evidence.
A stale candidate or superseded plan revision wins a concurrent publish race and becomes visible as current context.
The executing agent supplies or reuses approval evidence and promotes its own proposed memory without a distinct verified human.
Hermes local memory and Neon both act as writable authorities, producing conflicting current context without a canonical lineage.
A shared approximate-nearest-neighbor search retrieves foreign-scope vectors before post-filtering and leaks existence or ranking.
A backup restore or successor replay revives a forgotten memory without preserving the deletion marker and lineage.
